aricha-jamuna-riverside.desc: Aricha was once the main ferry crossing between Dhaka and the north-west, and nearby Paturia still runs ferries across the Padma to Daulatdia. Near here the Jamuna joins the Padma, so the water seems to stretch to the horizon. In the dry season, wide chars appear, and local boatmen take visitors out on them. The ghat restaurants serve fresh river fish.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Dhaka (Gabtoli) towards Aricha or Paturia ghat.
Good to know
Avoid boat trips in rough weather, especially in monsoon.

manikganj-date-palm-tapping.desc: Date-palm sap collection is one of rural Bengal's winter traditions, and in Manikganj it underpins the famous hazari gur. Gachhis shave the top of the trunk, fix a bamboo spout and hang a clay pot overnight. At dawn the sap is poured into wide pans and boiled for hours over straw fires. Watching the process early on a foggy morning is the best introduction to the district.
blocks: Good to know
Avoid drinking raw sap; it can carry Nipah virus. Try the boiled gur instead.

glance: About 400–600 BDT per kg depending on the sweet (2023)
Nizam's sweet shop at Terosree bazar, Ghior; outlets at Ghior Panch Rasta and Khalpar in Manikganj town
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
ghior-nizam-mishti.desc: Around 1965 Md. Nizamuddin, who ran a tea stall at Terosree bazar in Ghior upazila, started boiling leftover milk into a sweet and rolling it in mawa. It caught on after being served at a college event in 1966, and Manikganj people now simply call it Nizam's mishti. Fresh chhana is cooked in syrup, cooled and coated with milk mawa. The family's workshop also makes shahi chomchom, malai chop and sandesh.

teota-zamindar-bari.desc: Teota village in Shivalaya upazila holds the remains of a large zamindar estate. Its most striking feature is the Navaratna math, a tall temple with nine spires, built in the zamindar's courtyard. The palace buildings around it are weathered and partly ruined, which gives the place a quiet, melancholy beauty. It is close to the Aricha area and the Jamuna.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Dhaka towards Aricha/Shivalaya, then a local auto to Teota.
Good to know
Some buildings are unstable; stay out of cordoned areas.

dhankora-zamindar-bari.desc: The Roy Chowdhury family who founded the Dhankora estate in Saturia are said to have come from Delhi; Narasingha Roy Chowdhury was the founder, and the family held some two dozen revenue offices, with lands as far as present-day Mymensingh. Next to the house they set up a school named after Girishgobinda Roy Chowdhury. The family left for India in 1952. Few travellers come here, though it is only a short ride from Baliati Palace.
blocks: How to get there
From Saturia or Baliati take an auto or CNG to Dhankora village.
Good to know
Combine it with Baliati Palace in the same afternoon. Be respectful, as the school is still in use.

manikganj-river-fish.desc: Ghat-side eateries at Paturia and Aricha serve fish straight from the Padma and Jamuna. Fried hilsa, the national fish, is the favourite, eaten with hot rice and a little of the frying oil. Other river fish such as pangas, boal and small fish are cooked in thin, spicy curries. Prices depend on the size and season of the catch, so ask before ordering.
blocks: Good to know
Hilsa is best in the monsoon and early autumn; confirm the per-piece price first.

baliati-zamindar-bari.desc: The Baliati zamindar family rose from the salt trade in the 18th and 19th centuries and built this complex of several blocks in Saturia upazila. Grand two- and three-storey front buildings face a long courtyard with Corinthian columns and decorated pediments. One building is open as a small museum with period furniture. The complex is under the Department of Archaeology and is among the best-kept zamindar houses in the country.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Dhaka (Gabtoli) to Saturia, then a CNG or auto to Baliati, about 2–2.5 hours in total.
Good to know
Usually closed Sundays; check opening hours before going.

glance: 60 km to Manikganj by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
betila-zamindar-bari.desc: Betila, a few kilometres from Manikganj town, was once a busy stop for big country boats and trading vessels using the Betila canal. A wealthy trading family built this zamindar house there; local stories name a merchant called Jyoti Babu as an ancestor, but little is written down. Today the building, known locally as Satu Babu's house, is used as a government shelter centre. Its columned facade is still worth seeing on a zamindar-house tour with Baliati and Teota.
blocks: How to get there
From Manikganj town take an auto or CNG to Betila Mitara, a short ride south of town.
Good to know
It is a working government building, so ask before entering. Morning light is best for photos of the front.

glance: 60 km to Manikganj by road, 2–3 hours by bus or car
machain-shahi-mosque.desc: Machain Shahi Mosque stands in Machain village of Harirampur upazila, on the bank of the Ichamati, about 25 km from Manikganj town. Local history says Sultan Alauddin Husain Shah had it built around 1501 for the Sufi Shah Rustam Baghdadi, who is said to have prayed on a bamboo platform (machan) in the river, which gave the village its name. The three-domed mosque has been in use ever since and has been enlarged over the years. It is a protected monument of the Department of Archaeology, and the saint's shrine sits beside it.
blocks: How to get there
From Manikganj town take a bus or CNG to Jhitka or Harirampur, then an auto or CNG to Machain in Balla union.
Good to know
Dress modestly and avoid prayer times. The Ichamati banks nearby are pleasant in the late afternoon.

manikganj-mustard-fields.desc: Manikganj's low, flood-fed land is ideal for winter mustard, and from December into January whole stretches of country turn yellow. Beekeepers set out boxes along the field edges to collect mustard honey. The rural roads of Saturia, Ghior and Daulatpur are good for a slow drive or cycle. Go on a clear morning when the light is soft.
blocks: How to get there
Any rural road off the Dhaka–Aricha highway; hire a CNG for a few hours.
Good to know
Stay on the field edges and ask before walking through crops; buy fresh mustard honey from beekeepers.

glance: Jhitka area of Harirampur, and winter fairs in Manikganj town
manikganj-hazari-gur.desc: Hazari gur is made from the sap of date palms in Jhitka and Gopinathpur in Harirampur upazila, a tradition said to be about 350 years old. Gachhis tap the trees on cold nights and the sap is boiled down at dawn and beaten into light, crumbly cakes with a delicate aroma. It received Geographical Indication status, and fewer families make it now, so the real thing is prized. Eat it with muri or in winter pitha.
blocks: Good to know
Buy directly from makers to avoid adulterated gur.
